question: Does RIAL causally support the persistent SMD/body rhythm through its existing chemical RIAL-to-SMD route, and is the influence reversible?
motivation: E083 identifies RIAL as largest sampled rhythmic chemical input to ventral SMD, but does not establish causal necessity or isolated oscillator identity
fixed: All302-neuron parameters/topology/kinetics/reversals, NMJ weights/signs/transfer, sensory mappings and body/water mechanics; original checkpoints and input files unchanged
screen_cases: RIAR counterpart membrane conductance.1nS at-80mV; no assumption it is inert
Hold existing RIAL-to-SMD chemical release at RIAL's own selected-sham20..30s mean
Hold existing RIAL-to-ventral-SMD chemical release at that mean
Set release on existing RIAL-to-ventral-SMD chemical edges to0 as a tonic-plus-rhythmic transmission control
branch_implementation: Sparse existing-edge override at every neural substep: replace g[post,pre]*release(pre) by g[post,pre]*held_probability and adjust both total conductance and weighted-reversal drive. No new edge, reversal change, externally negative conductance, NMJ hold or voltage freeze. RIAL voltage/other outputs/gap junctions remain live; secondary network/body-feedback changes are allowed. Only existing targets included, actual post/pre indices and held probabilities recorded.
timing: Eight60s screens, interventions30..40s. Baseline20..30s, response35..40s, recovery50..60s. Select best safe RIAL membrane condition prioritizing confirmed hyperpolarization/recovery then body attenuation, plus predeclared RIAL-to-SMD mean-release branch.
confirmation: Both selected interventions plus shared matched sham, repeated120s(30..40 and80..90 holds) and long-hold150s(30..90 hold,130..150 recovery):6 trials
refinement: Both interventions plus shared sham at neural-half and body-half:6 nominal trials. Controls cannot be selected as RIAL membrane winner. Total20 planned trials.

criteria.source: Hash-verified capsule/model/traces; full coordinate vector reconstructs pinned model. Ordinary sham and pre-intervention prefixes match original<=1e-8; same-grid paired prefix and finite/safe state checks inherited from E082.
criteria.recovery: Active/recovery regional cycles>=max(.003rad,.8matched sham), regional cadence1.62..1.98Hz; no requirement of exact post-intervention phase
criteria.membrane_access: RIAL mean hyperpolarization>=5mV; reported separately and not demanded of branch holds
criteria.branch: Declared existing-edge release replacement, probabilities0..1, duplicate/absent branches rejected, outside selected interval inactive identity. Branch intervention does not require RIAL voltage or neural variability to be suppressed.
criteria.effect: Report body range and downstream ventral-SMD centered-voltage RMS ratios separately. Prospective reversible-body-attenuation flag requires<=.2body/sham with pre/safety/recovery on nominal and all confirmations/refinements; separate downstream-variance flag<=.2SMD/sham. Strict1e-4rad rest retained as a separate diagnostic.
criteria.numerical: Two refined body/SMD RMS ratio differences<=.05 for EACH of the two selected interventions; both flags require these consistency checks. Completion alone is not a positive effect.
criteria.qualification: No learned stopping, sensory start/stop, swimming, biological fidelity or isolated RIAL pacemaker qualification

interpretation_rules: Mean-release branch suppression would support causal contribution of rhythmic transmission under this operating point. Zero-release-only suppression could involve tonic support or operating-point change. Whole-neuron suppression without branch effect could involve other RIAL routes/feedback. Persistence may involve redundancy/compensation; no single result establishes universal or biological necessity.
